title: Slab Unwind and Crew Compression Playbook
content:
Executive summary

This working playbook outlines a conservative approach to unwinding slab/commitment discounts and compressing crew (hiring freeze + phased contractor reduction) to protect runway while minimizing customer disruption. It contains: assumptions, a three-scenario simulation, a month-by-month HC phasing CSV for core roles, pricing sensitivity delta table, operational triggers for credit/ burst pools, and a short runbook for customer outreach.

Why this exists
- Observed: accelerating token cost pressure + commitments that lock price/volume are creating margin risk into H2 2027.
- Goal: reduce burn by 10–18% over 6 months while preserving SLA for top-tier customers and offering clear transitional pricing for mid-market.
- Constraint: limited headcount moves — prefer natural attrition and contract step-downs; avoid mass layoffs unless tail risk realized.

Key assumptions
- Base ARR growth remains at 28% year-over-year for model baseline.
- Token unit cost (effective after GPU mix improvements) currently $0.0009; model run tests +/− 20%.
- 60% of slab customers on auto-renew; 40% can be offered a managed unwind (credits + gentle price rise).
- Hiring pipeline frozen for non-critical roles starting 2026-12-01.

Scenario matrix (6-month lens)
1) Gentle taper (preferred): unwind discounts on renewals only, offer one-time credit cushion equal to 6 weeks of committed tokens. HC: idle hires paused; contractors reduced 10% by attrition. Estimated burn delta: −10%.
2) Targeted unwind (balanced): proactively approach 30% of slab customers with new pricing tiers; use 12-week credit buffer for 20% of accounts. HC: contractors reduced 25% by planned off-ramps; 2 product hires deferred. Estimated burn delta: −14%.
3) Rapid compression (defensive): immediate slab reset for new signups + 30% of renewals; aggressive contractor ramp-down and hiring pause across teams. HC: target 8% role consolidation (voluntary severance package prepared). Estimated burn delta: −18% (fast) with elevated churn risk.

Trigger rules (activation matrix)
- Trigger A: 3-week rolling loss of committed revenue >= 4% -> escalate to scenario 2 playbook and open customer remediation channels.
- Trigger B: token unit cost +20% vs baseline for 4 consecutive weeks -> activate Rapid compression holdback on non-essential infra spend.
- Trigger C: runway horizon <= 9 months at current burn -> immediate exec review and implement Rapid compression.

Note: lines prefixed with '>' are teams prioritized for conservative staffing pressure (higher contractor mix).

Pricing sensitivity (summary)
- Method: simulate price change on slab floor and new negotiated tiers, estimate demand elasticity using cohort response rates from Q2 renewals.
- Elasticities used: enterprise cohort −0.08 (inelastic), mid-market −0.45, self-serve −1.1.
- Quick table (price delta -> estimated net rev impact over 6 months):
  +10% price -> enterprise +3% rev, mid-market −4% rev, self-serve −9% rev; net approx +1.5% rev on portfolio baseline.
  +20% price -> enterprise +5% rev, mid-market −9% rev, self-serve −18% rev; net approx −3.5% rev.
  Price floor removal (unwind slab to list) -> churn risk concentrated in mid-market; expected 12–16% churn in that cohort with large initial revenue drop then partial recovery over 9 months.

Operational levers and customer offers
- Credit cushion: 6–12 weeks of committed usage credits to soften renewal shock; funded from short-term reserve bucket.
- Phased quota gating: for repeat high-cost customers, enable tiered throttles as fallback to avoid immediate infra spin-up costs.
- Migration assistance: offer a free 1-week migration to quantized models + consult for customers on Dedicated to reduce token spend.
- Contract amendments: standard addendum template drafted (linked_artifacts above).

Financial modelling notes (spreadsheet-friendly guidance)
- Model width: run 3 levers independently and combined: price change, contractor reduction rate, and token unit cost delta.
- Time horizon: 6 months primary, 12 months sensitivity for downstream churn effects.
- KPI focus: net burn change, ARR retention delta, gross margin %, and runway months.

Risks and mitigations
- Customer churn: mitigate with credits + hands-on outreach for top-20 accounts. Escalation to AE + Solutions Eng mandatory for accounts > $250K ARR.
- Talent flight: emphasize voluntary programs, hiring freezes only for non-critical roles, and redeployment before cuts.
- Reputational: coordinate comms with marketing and legal; produce templated FAQ for account teams.

Open questions / decisions needed
1) Approval to fund a temporary credits reserve of $2.5M — finance to sign-off. (JIRA FIN-7892)
2) Level of contractor reduction to model as base-case (10% vs 25%).
3) Which product features are gated under tiered throttles? Ops + Product decision.

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Finance: finalize reserve sizing and post commit to runbook (owner: Samir).
- Sales Ops: identify top 120 slab accounts and assign outreach owners (owner: Lina).
- People Ops: draft voluntary separation and redeployment play templates (owner: Trevor).
- Modeling: produce a 12 month sensitivity workbook (gsheet:capacity-forecast-2026) with scenario toggles (owner: Nora).

Appendix: quick decision checklist for exec review
- Is runway below 12 months? Y/N
- Is token cost trending up >10% q/q? Y/N
- Can we fund credits reserve without changing hiring headcount? Y/N
- If 2 or more answers are Y -> recommend escalate to Rapid compression within 7 days.

Notes to reviewers
- This is deliberately conservative and assumes limited upside in token price. Please annotate modelling assumptions directly in the linked gsheet.
- This doc is a working playbook; expect iteration after modeling outputs and top-customer outreach feedback.
